THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE H.T. NARENDRA PRASAD  ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

This appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act')
has been filed by the claimant challenging by the judgment dated 20.09.2018 passed by MACT,
Bengaluru in MVC No.6005/2016.

2. Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that on 13.02.2016 at about 12.30 p.m., the claimant was riding his motorcycle bearing Registration No.KA-04-HV-1089 on NH-75 Bengaluru-Yediyur Road towards Yediyur with moderate speed, following all traffic rules by the left side of the road, at that time, the driver of the Car bearing Registration No.KA-51-MC-6786 drove the same from the same direction with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, endanger to human life and dashed against the claimant's bike from behind.

As a result of the NC:
2024:KHC:37685 aforesaid accident, the claimant sustained grievous injuries and was hospitalized.
3. The claimant filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act, seeking compensation.
It was pleaded that he spent significant amount towards medical expenses, conveyance charges and other related costs.
It was further pleaded that the accident occurred solely on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
4. Upon service of notice, the respondent No.1 appeared through counsel and filed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.

The respondent No.2, despite service of notice,
did not appear before the Tribunal and was placed ex-parte.

5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter,
recorded the evidence.

The Tribunal, by impugned judgment and award has partly allowed the claim petition and held that NC: 2024:KHC:37685 the claimant is entitled to a compensation of Rs.2,62,200/- along with interest at the rate of 8% p.a. and directed the Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.
Being aggrieved, the present appeal has been filed.

sentences.text:
The learned counsel for the claimant has raised the following contentions:
a) Firstly, the claimant asserts that he was earning Rs.25,356/- per month by working as an Executive in Anvase Exim Private Company.
To prove the same, he produced Ex.P8-Salary Certificate.

However, the Tribunal has erred in taking the income as merely as Rs.15,000/-
per month.
b) Secondly, the claimant has examined the doctor as PW-2.
The doctor, in his evidence, has deposed that the claimant suffered 15.57% disability.
Due to this disability, the claimant is under threat of being dismissed from service by his employer.

However, the Tribunal has not NC:
2024:KHC:37685 awarded any compensation under the head of loss of future income due to disability.
c) Lastly, due to the accident, the claimant has sustained grievous injuries.
He was treated as inpatient for a period of 10 days.
Even after discharge from the hospital, he was not in a position to discharge his regular work.
He has suffered lot of pain during treatment.

Considering the same, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the heads of 'loss of amenities', 'pain and sufferings'
and other incidental expenses are on the lower side.
With the above contentions, the learned counsel sought to allow the appeal.

7. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the Insurance Company has raised the following counter- contentions:
a) Firstly, although the claimant alleged that he was earning Rs.25,356/- per month and produced his Salary Certificate (Ex.P8) in support, he failed to examine the NC:
2024:KHC:37685 author of the document.
Therefore, the Tribunal has assessed the claimant's income notionally.

b) Secondly, although the doctor testified that the claimant suffered a 15.57%
disability, the claimant (PW-1) admitted in his evidence that he has continued in his employment.
Till today the claimant has not produced any documents to show that he has been discontinued from his service.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly not granted any compensation under the head of loss of income due to disability.

c) Thirdly, considering the injuries sustained by the claimant and considering the age and avocation of the claimant, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the heads of 'loss of amenities', 'pain and sufferings' and other incidental expenses are just and reasonable and it does not warrant interference.

d) Lastly, in light of the Division Bench decision of this Court in the case of Ms.Joyeeta Bose and others -v- Sri K Siddaramanna vs Future General India Insurance Co Ltd on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152208242/
3 Venkateshan.

entities.text: Joyeeta Bose and others -v- Sri K Siddaramanna vs Future General India Insurance Co Ltd on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: V and others (MFA 5896/2018 and connected matters disposed of on 24.8.2020), the NC: 2024:KHC:37685 rate of interest awarded by the Tribunal at 8% p.a. on the compensation amount
appears excessive.
With the above contentions, the learned counsel sought to dismiss the appeal.
8. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal and original records.
9. It is not in dispute that the claimant has sustained injuries in the road traffic accident occurred on 13.02.2016 due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
10. The claimant was working as Executive in Anvase Exim Private Company and was earning Rs.25,356/- per month and he has produced Salary Certificate at Ex.P8.
Considering the evidence of PW-1 and Ex.P8, the monthly income of the claimant can be considered Rs.25,000/- after deducted profession tax.
The loss of income during the laid up period can be granted for four months with the NC: 2024:KHC:37685 monthly income of Rs.25,000/- that comes to Rs.1,00,000/-.
11. As per wound certificate, the claimant has sustained fracture of left femur and fibula, fracture of Basal neck of Fibula.
The claimant has examined the doctor as PW-2.
Although the doctor testified that the claimant suffered 15.57% disability, he has not assessed the limb disability.
Since the claimant has admitted that he has been continued in his job, even today he has not produced any document to prove that he has been removed from his service.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly not awarded any compensation under the head of 'loss of future income'.
However, due to the disability, the claimant has suffered lot of pain during the treatment and he has to suffer this disability through out of his life.

Considering the prolonged pain during treatment as well as the permanent disability certified by the doctor, I am of the opinion that the claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- under the head of 'disability'.
Although the evidence of the doctor suggests that the claimant requires approximately Rs.80,000/- for removal of implants, the claimant has not provided any estimate for future surgery.

Considering the nature of the injuries and the evidence of the doctor, I am inclined to enhance the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head of 'future medical expenses' from Rs.30,000/- to Rs.40,000/-.
13. Considering the nature of injuries, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads is just and reasonable.

14. Thus, the claimant is entitled to the following compensation:
